sm.comment: The height of a control, in the approved design's control rhythm: a button is 30px and a small one 26px, and an icon button, a field in a toolbar and a segmented well stand at the same 30px, so every control on a line shares one height. The small step carries a floor because 26 x 0.82 is 21.32px, and a target under 24px fails at compact density on a touch screen. Every step is emitted as calc(Npx * var(--density, 1)), so it is unchanged at density 1.

md.comment: The design's button, icon button, toolbar field and segmented well. A chip inside a well is six under it: a 1px boundary and a 2px inset on each side, which leaves exactly the 24px target floor at density 1.

sm.comment: The height of a list row, so every list in a product lines up with every other. The small step floors at 24px as the control step does.

gutter.comment: The rail's geometry in TWO parts, because a row's EDGE and a row's TEXT want different insets. The gutter insets the rail, which is where a row's background begins; the row pad insets the content inside the row. Splitting it is what lets the rows widen without moving a glyph: shrink the gutter, grow the pad by the same step, and the line every mark, group label and item text starts on does not move.

row.comment: The height of a row in the rail: a destination, a project, a pinned view. The approved design draws it at 30px, the control rhythm's own height, and a rail row is a step of its own rather than size.row.md (36px, a list's row) because a rail holds fifteen destinations and more in a column the height of the window, where six pixels a row is the difference between the last one on screen and behind the foot. No floor is needed: 30 x 0.82 is 24.6px, over the 24px target at every density.

rail.comment: The application SHELL's geometry, in the approved design's numbers. The rail is the sidebar column, on the frame; breakpoint.shell is derived from it, so a change here moves that step too, and the AppShell suite holds the arithmetic. A fixed width at every density: the rail's rows and gutters scale inside it, and a rail that grew with the density would move the breakpoint the density does not.

topbar.comment: The top bar of the sheet, and the rail's head beside it, which stands at the same height so the first nav row starts level with the top of the screen. A side sheet's head (Modal variant="sheet") stands at it too, on the line the bar behind it draws. Fixed at every density, like the rail.

inset.comment: The gap between the frame's edge and the floating sheet, on its top, its inline end and its bottom; the rail is the gap on the inline start. Density-scaled like every other gap, so it is 6.56px compact and 9.12px comfortable; breakpoint.shell is derived at density 1. It belongs to the wide layout: under breakpoint.shell the design's sheet is full-bleed, with no inset and no corner.

targetMin.comment: The smallest a hit target may ever stand, and the same floor size.control.sm and size.row.sm carry. It is a token because a component that DERIVES a height from a control step (a chip in a well stands shorter than the control beside it) has to clamp the result itself: max(var(--size-target-min), calc(...)) holds at every density, where the step's own floor no longer can once it has been subtracted from.

measure.comment: Prose and forms get a measure. Tables and charts deliberately do not: they are the one content that genuinely wants the whole viewport.

focusRingInsetOffset.comment: The outline offset for a focusable row INSIDE a clipping scroller: a tree row, a grid row, a card header. An outset ring there is clipped by the scroller on the first and last rows and painted over by the next row, so the indicator has to be drawn inside the row's own box.
